root_cause.text: An off-by-one error in the second memcpy call within `lowpan_iphc_mcast_ctx_addr_compress()` where the destination offset `&data[1]` and source offset `&ipaddr->s6_addr[11]` should have been `&data[2]` and `&ipaddr->s6_addr[12]` respectively, causing corruption of the RIID field and leakage of uninitialized kernel stack memory over the network.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the fix changes `memcpy(&data[1], &ipaddr->s6_addr[11], 4)` to `memcpy(&data[2], &ipaddr->s6_addr[12], 4)`, and adds zero-initialization of the `data` array. The commit message explicitly states: "The second memcpy in lowpan_iphc_mcast_ctx_addr_compress() uses &data[1] as destination and &ipaddr->s6_addr[11] as source, but both should be offset by one: &data[2] and &ipaddr->s6_addr[12] respectively. This off-by-one has two consequences: ... data[5] is never written, so uninitialized kernel stack memory is transmitted over the network via lowpan_push_hc_data(), leaking kernel stack contents."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix overlapping memcpy and incorrect source offsets in 6LoWPAN multicast address compression to produce correct compressed header according to RFC 6282.
intent_record.what: Initialized local array 'data' to zero; changed second memcpy destination offset from &data[1] to &data[2] and source offset from s6_addr[11] to s6_addr[12].
intent_record.how: Zero-initialization prevents using uninitialized data; corrected offsets ensure the 2-byte flags/scope and 4-byte group ID are placed sequentially without overlap and using the correct bytes (last 4 bytes of the group ID).

grouping_result.intent: Fix overlapping memcpy and incorrect source offsets in 6LoWPAN multicast address compression to produce correct compressed header according to RFC 6282.
